about: Hand-kept triage of concerns about PROJ itself, read by report/proj_concerns.py. Only a person changes an entry's status. 'signals' lists the automatic signals (roundtrip, consensus) an entry accounts for, per projection id, so they leave the untriaged list. 'proj_links' holds only issues, pull requests or commits in OSGeo/PROJ; an entry without one has not been sent to PROJ.

statuses.suspected: flagged, not yet looked at closely
statuses.confirmed: reproduced with a minimal case outside the benchmark
statuses.drafted: a fix and a test exist; not filed
statuses.reported: filed with PROJ by a person (link given)
statuses.not-a-bug: looked at; PROJ is right or the difference is by design

concerns.title: ortho: ellipsoidal oblique inverse fails or lands wrong with k_0 != 1 or alpha != 0
concerns.detail: `ortho_e_inverse()` unrotates by alpha and divides by k_0, then seeds Newton with `ortho_s_inverse()`, which does both again. With k_0 = 0.9 about 44% of inverses fail; with alpha the seed can converge to the wrong point. A patch and a gie test exist (they move the unrotate and scale out of the spherical inverse into a wrapper). Not in this suite, which uses k_0 = 1 and no alpha.

concerns.title: ortho: ellipsoidal inverse returns inf at and next to a visible pole
concerns.detail: With `+proj=ortho +ellps=WGS84 +lat_0=-42 +lon_0=147` the south pole is on the visible side. Forward gives (0, -4745251.365); the inverse of that returns (inf, inf), as it does for lat -89.9999999. At lat -89.99 the round trip is fine, and the spherical case (`+R=6371000`) inverts the pole. Cause not yet traced; the oblique branch of `ortho_e_inverse()` near the pole is the first place to look. Separate from the k_0 entry: with k_0 = 1 and no alpha that patch does not change the seed.

concerns.title: moll: forward x at the poles is 112.5 m, not 0
concerns.detail: At lon -180 lat -90, PROJ gives x = -112.5 m where the exact answer is 0 (every meridian meets at the pole). proj4rs, wbprojection, proj4js and math.gl all give 0. In `moll_s_forward()` the Newton step for the auxiliary angle divides by 1 + cos(theta), which goes to 0 at the pole, so convergence there is slow; the loop exits on its step-size test with theta still short of pi/2, and cos(theta) is not quite 0.

concerns.title: eqearth: PROJ's round trip at the poles is 6.6e-6 deg off
concerns.detail: Forward then inverse of lat -90 returns lat -89.9999934. Cause not yet traced: the inverse's Newton tolerance is 1e-11, so the loss is elsewhere, perhaps the clamp of y to MAX_Y or the authalic latitude conversion near the pole. Small, but larger than any other round trip in the suite.

concerns.title: World projections: inverse refuses points exactly on lon +-180 or at a pole
concerns.detail: Every inverse failure in these is on the outline of the map: lon +-180, or a pole that the projection draws as a point or a line. One step inside (lon 179.9999999 for wag4) inverts correctly. Most likely deliberate range checks that reject the boundary itself; still to check whether that is intended.

concerns.title: eqc: PROJ is ellipsoidal since 2026-01, the ports are spherical
concerns.detail: PROJ added the ellipsoidal Equidistant Cylindrical method (EPSG 1028) in 6a529ad4; the ports still use the spherical formulas, so they agree with each other and differ from PROJ by 29 km. PROJ is right; this is a porting gap.

concerns.title: ortho: three ports agree with each other and differ from PROJ by 33.7 km
concerns.detail: wbprojection, proj4js and math.gl compute ortho on a sphere of radius a. PROJ has used ellipsoidal formulas since 7.2. PROJ is right.

concerns.title: omerc: gamma-only definitions become alpha = 0 through pyproj's Proj()/CRS route
concerns.detail: A `+proj=omerc` string with `+gamma` and no `+alpha` comes back from `pyproj.Proj()` or `CRS()` with `+alpha=0` added, which changes the projection. `Transformer.from_pipeline` keeps the string as given, which is why the benchmark uses it. Not yet narrowed down to pyproj or to PROJ's CRS layer.
